title: height:100% is inert inside a padding-driven aspect-ratio shell (content height 0) — measured px or a different shell must be chosen
trigger: Wrapping/resizing a player shell collapses the video to h:0 on sites that size the player box with padding-top instead of a real height (m.youtube #player.player-size; common legacy aspect-ratio trick)
principle: Percentage heights resolve against the parent's CONTENT height — a box built as `height:0; padding-top:56.25%` has content height 0, so height:100% on any in-flow descendant resolves to 0 and the whole stage collapses (absolute-positioned descendants still resolve against the padding box, which is why the video looked fine before wrapping). When picking a shell to restructure, prefer the ancestor with a real computed height (on m.youtube the same-size walk reaches #player-container-id — position:fixed, definite height — which also owns the sibling control overlays). Desktop-only selectors/short-circuits (e.g. #movie_player) may exist on the mobile DOM too but with different positioning semantics — gate them on the mobile-shell marker, don't assume id equality means layout equality.

cases.context: m.youtube split view: playerShell resolved to #movie_player (absolute inside #player.player-size, content h:0). Wrapper inserted in-flow → height:100% of 0 → stageCell 210×0, video black, cue panel painted over the player box.

applyFor: Feature code that wraps/moves a site's player shell (split view, player mode, layout injection)
Debugging 'element h:0 after moving' on mobile web players
Choosing between a short-circuit id match and the generic same-size walk — verify the mobile variant's box model first
